title: Update from Freedom House CEO Jamie Fly: New Partnerships and Opportunities to Stand for Freedom
content:
This fall brought new partnerships and new opportunities to stand with those on the front lines of the fight for freedom.

Carnegie Council for Ethics in International Affairs

In September, I joined Carnegie Council President Joel Rosenthal in New York for Carnegie’s Values and Interests series. We discussed why democracy is both a moral and a political principle, the regression of freedom globally, and what can be done to counter the new wave of autocrats and illiberal actors.

title: Joint Statement for the International Day of Political Prisoners on October 30
content:
The October 30 Coalition have released the following joint statement to rally support for political prisoners and champion their freedom. The joint statement highlights the importance of sustained international attention to individual political prisoners, efforts to secure their release, and accountability for abuses. The October 30 Coalition consists of the 30 October Foundation, Free Russia Foundation, Free Them One by One, Freedom House, the Human Rights Foundation, the Lantos Foundation, the McCain Institute, the National Endowment for Democracy, the Raoul Wallenberg Centre for Human Rights, and World Liberty Congress. Organizations interested in signing the joint statement can fill out this form.

Joint Statement for the International Day of Political Prisoners on October 30

On this International Day of Political Prisoners, we stand together to affirm a simple truth: no one should be imprisoned for speaking freely, standing up for their beliefs, or exercising their fundamental rights.

title: Roll Call for Freedom: A Ceremony Honoring Political Prisoners
content:
Register 


Around the world, journalists, civic leaders, artists, religious figures, and others are imprisoned for exercising fundamental freedoms. Behind every name is a person whose imprisonment has separated families, silenced vital voices, and deprived communities of courageous leadership.

To mark the International Day of Political Prisoners, Freedom House, the October 30 Coalition, and the National Endowment for Democracy invite the public to gather at the Lincoln Memorial for a ceremony honoring political prisoners and those working for their freedom.

During the event, participants will read the names of prisoners from countries across the world, ensuring that their stories are heard in the heart of the nation’s capital.

The ceremony will also recognize those released during the past year and remember those who died in forced detention. It will conclude with a joint call for free people everywhere to defend the rights of political prisoners, press for their release, and support their families.

title: Vilnius Freedom Summit Unites Democratic Leaders and Activists Across Regions
content:
Vilnius, Lithuania—Freedom House and the Lithuanian Ministry of Foreign Affairs co-hosted the Vilnius Freedom Summit today, bringing together senior government officials, Nobel Peace Prize laureates, former political prisoners, and democracy advocates to strengthen international cooperation in confronting authoritarian threats. Hosted at Lithuania’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the summit emphasized the urgent need for greater coordination among democracies as authoritarian governments increasingly work together to suppress dissent and undermine democratic institutions.

“The desire for freedom is universal, and those standing up to authoritarian rule face many of the same challenges, regardless of where they live,” said Jamie Fly, CEO of Freedom House. “Lithuania, with its own history of overcoming Soviet occupation and longstanding tradition of solidarity with those fighting for freedom, was a fitting place to bring frontline activists from Central and Eastern Europe and Latin America together with policymakers, to strengthen cooperation and support one another in this shared struggle.”

title: Freedom House Adopts Cases of Imprisoned Vietnamese Journalists Le Anh Hung and Pham Chi Dung
content:
Washington, DC—Freedom House announced today that the Fred Hiatt Program to Free Political Prisoners has adopted the cases of imprisoned Vietnamese journalists Le Anh Hung and Pham Chi Dung, both of whom were formerly affiliated with the international multimedia broadcaster Voice of America.

“Freedom House is proud to stand with Le Anh Hung and Pham Chi Dung and fight for their release,” said Jamie Fly, CEO of Freedom House. “Vietnam has one of the most restrictive media environments in the world, with independent journalists routinely detained, prosecuted, and imprisoned. We call for Le Anh Hung and Pham Chi Dung to be immediately and unconditionally released.”

Le Anh Hung is an independent journalist who published articles on a range of topics, including politics and corruption, for a variety of independent media outlets, including Voice of America. He was arrested by Vietnamese authorities on March 9, 2026, and has been detained since. He is charged with "propaganda against the state," which carries a sentence of up to 20 years in prison. He was previously imprisoned from 2018 to 2023 for “abusing democratic freedoms to infringe upon the interests of the state.”

title: Vilnius Freedom Summit Statement
content:
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Lithuania, together with Freedom House, is proud to host the Vilnius Freedom Summit, bringing together democratic governments, civil society leaders, human rights defenders, independent journalists, and former political prisoners. At a time when authoritarian regimes are increasingly coordinating across borders, sharing repressive tactics, technologies, propaganda tactics, and political support, democracies must respond with equal unity and determination. 

We reaffirm our commitment to supporting those on the front lines of freedom and democracy worldwide. Lithuania knows from its own history that democracy cannot be defended within national borders alone. We remain grateful for the principled position of the United States, including the Welles Declaration, during our struggle for freedom, and we know how important international solidarity is for those who continue to fight for their rights and liberties today.

title: Joint Statement by Human Rights Organizations regarding Abduction of Human Rights Defenders
content:
We, the undersigned organizations, condemn in strongest possible terms the abduction of three human rights defenders by Vietnamese authorities in Cambodia and their subsequent arbitrary detention in Vietnam.

The Vietnamese government must immediately and unconditionally release Nguyen Duc Thuan, a Norwegian citizen, Tran Hiep (Ho Pham Hiep Huy), an Australian citizen, and Thai Cong Truong Son, an ethnic Vietnamese living in Cambodia. Pending their release, Norwegian and Australian consular officials must be granted immediate access to Mr. Thuan and Mr. Hiep.

Background

Mr. Thuan and Mr. Hiep went missing on the morning of 18 September 2026 while traveling to the Kaoh Andaet area of Cambodia. For ten days, they were incommunicado.

On 28 September, Vietnam’s Ministry of Public Security announced that the three men had been caught “illegally entering Vietnam” at the My Quy Tay Border Gate on 18 September. Subsequently, the three men are currently being investigated for “terrorism”. Their families and colleagues strongly reject this account. All available information points to the fact that the men were abducted on Cambodian soil and forcibly taken across the border.

title: The Belarusian People Deserve to be Free: Remarks by Freedom House CEO Jamie Fly
content:
Freedom House CEO Jamie Fly joined Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, the leader of Belarus’s democratic movement, along with senior officials from the European Union, the Council of Europe, Estonia, Ireland, Latvia, Lithuania, Sweden, and Ukraine for a UN General Assembly side event focused on the threat that Lukashenka’s autocratic regime poses to regional and international security. 

His remarks, addressing Lukashenka’s repression, Freedom House’s role in assisting Belarusian political prisoners, and the importance of a free and democratic Belarus, follow.

Jamie Fly: It’s an honor to be here today with so many staunch transatlantic allies of the United States and strong advocates for freedom, including Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, whose leadership and continued advocacy on behalf of the Belarusian people is critical to the country’s democratic future.

title: Political Prisoners Watch: Five Democracy Advocates Targeted for Seeking Help Abroad
content:
From left to right: Pham Chi Dung, Anar Mammadli, Joshua Wong, Mohammad Seifzadeh, Gasser Abdel Razek (Photo Credits: Pham Chi Dung Facebook, Wikimedia Commons, Center for Human Rights in Iran, Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights)

On September 2, prominent Hong Kong democracy activist Joshua Wong pleaded guilty to charges under the territory’s notorious National Security Act—the second time he has faced prison time under the Beijing-imposed law. Having already been imprisoned since November 2020, he now faces the possibility of another lengthy sentence simply for demanding that Hong Kongers have a voice in their own government. Joshua’s detention has been widely recognized as emblematic of the Chinese Communist Party’s increasing restrictions on freedom in and the autonomy of Hong Kong.

title: REPORT LAUNCH: Freedom on the Net 2026
content:
Register


Join Freedom House for the launch of Freedom on the Net 2026: Seismic Shifts on the Global Internet. Following a presentation on key findings from the 2026 report, experts will discuss global trends, country-specific developments, and best practices for how to protect internet freedom.

Speakers include:

  • Mahsa Alimardani, Digital Rights Researcher and Advocate
  • Jennifer Brody, Deputy Director, Policy and Advocacy for Technology and Democracy, Freedom House
  • Jamie Fly, CEO, Freedom House
  • Justin Hendrix, CEO and Editor, Tech Policy Press 
  • David Peterson, General Manager, Proton VPN, Proton
